speaker: Doctor
text: Those blood counts and CRP levels are normal, which suggests your recurrent bronchitis may be non-infectious or driven by an underlying structural issue rather than a systemic infection. Since the fevers were absent and the inflammation markers are quiet, has your cough been worse in the morning or evening, and do you ever cough up mucus or see streaks of blood?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old woman. The patient has been experiencing an aggressive cough producing copious amounts of thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for about 11 years, with exacerbations similar to the current presentation today. Reports that the cough is worse in the morning and has had multiple evaluations in the past due to recurrent bouts of bronchitis requiring antibiotics treatment. The patient is a non-smoker.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Bronchiectasis

The presence of copious, thick, foamy, yellow-green sputum for 11 years, worsening in the morning, in a non-smoker is highly suggestive of bronchiectasis despite the normal inflammatory markers. Please confirm if you have ever been told you have "swan neck deformities" on your lungs or if you have had any episodes of hemoptysis.
